newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's Mobutu gives up powers but retains title.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu gives up powers but retains title.

text.p: Zaire's ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko, who left his capital on Friday, will no longer take any part in the government of the country, an official statement said.

Government spokesman Kin-Kiey Mulumba told a news conference after an "important" cabinet meeting on the transition of power in Zaire: "The president...has ceased all intervention in the affairs of the state."

In a lengthy and detailed statement citing constitutional clauses to underpin Mobutu's latest move, Kin-Kiey made clear that the government of Zaire was now in the hands of Prime Minister Likulia Bolongo.

The Archbishop of Kisangani, Monsignor Laurent Monsengwo, chosen a week ago as mediator, would undertake negotiations with the rebel alliance of Laurent Kabila, leading to a new transitional government and later fresh elections, Kin-Kiey said.
Citing a constitution that has been in effect for the past three years, the spokesman said Zairean law permitted Mobutu to effectively step aside without actually resigning as president.

"If the parties to the conflict, in particular the rebel alliance, act in good faith, the president's important decision to stand aside, coupled with the constraints which the constitution imposes...this will allow us to find a satisfactory compromise between the positions of the belligerents," the spokesman said.

Earlier on Friday state television said that Mobutu, who has been fighting prostate cancer and a seven-month-old civil war, had left Kinshasa for his northern jungle palace at Gbadolite on doctors' orders.
The spokesman confirmed that Mobutu had gone to Gbadolite but gave no further details.
The departure from Kinshasa of the man who has dominated Africa's third largest country for over three decades triggered intense speculation that he was on his way into exile.

Political and diplomatic sources said Mobutu's departure followed talks with army chiefs who told him they could not defend the capital against Kabila's advancing rebel forces and that he should leave for his own safety.
A Western diplomat in Morocco said Mobutu was expected there in the next 48 hours. "It seems that he has chosen Morocco as a place for exile," the diplomat said.
"I am hearing that Morocco is a likely first stop, with France as a final destination," one Western diplomat in Paris said. France declined all comment.
